children: Malaysian palm oil futures opened higher on Friday and are on track for a weekly gain after last week's decline, as firmer crude oil prices and rival Dalian oils supported the market.

The benchmark palm oil contract (FCPOc3) for November delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange gained 40 ringgit, or 0.82%, to 4,944 ringgit ($1,223.76) a metric ton in early trade. The contract has risen 0.35% so far this week.
FUNDAMENTALS
Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) rose 0.41%, while its palm oil contract
added 0.16%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (BOcv1) were down 0.07%.
Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.
Oil prices rose and are on track for their steepest weekly gain since mid-July as rising tensions and renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities heightened concerns over Middle East supply risks.
Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.
The ringgit
, palm's currency of trade, weakened 0.04% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies.
Indonesian state-owned plantation company Agrinas Palma Nusantara is targeting palm oil output of 1.5 million metric tons next year, said chief executive Mohammad Abdul Ghani.

Indonesia's effort to exert control over global prices for its vast natural resources by setting up a new commodities exchange will struggle to compete with established bourses and risks backfiring if participation is mandatory.
Malaysia's palm oil inventories are set to rise to a seven-month high in August, driven by the strongest production in nine months and a decline in exports, a Reuters survey showed.
Palm oil may retrace further to 4,850 ringgit per metric ton, as suggested by a rising trendline and a retracement analysis, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said.
MARKET NEWS

Asian shares rose on Friday as investors embraced a global rally before crucial U.S. jobs data, while bonds found some much needed relief after a top Federal Reserve official cooled rate hike fears and dragged the dollar lower. MKTS/GLOB
